abel-2.title: Abel
abel-2.note: Not Cain's brother. In these two verses Abel is a place: the great stone of Abel in a Beth-shemite's field where the ark came to rest, and a short form of the northern city people went to for good advice.

abiel-2.title: Abiel
abiel-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
abiel-2.note: Kish's father, which makes him Saul's grandfather. One of David's warriors carried the name as well. Nothing connects the two men but the spelling.

abijah-2.title: Abijah
abijah-2.about: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
abijah-2.note: A levite from the united kingdom. 1 Samuel and 1 Chronicles name him twice.

abinadab-2.title: Abinadab
abinadab-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
abinadab-2.note: The man whose house held the ark. It sat there twenty years before David came for it.

amorite.title: Amorite
amorite.note: One of the peoples in Canaan before Israel came, traced in Genesis 10 to a son of Canaan, and sometimes used loosely for everyone in the hill country. Sihon and Og ruled an Amorite kingdom east of the Jordan that fell to Israel under Moses. Outside the Bible they are the Amurru of Mesopotamian texts, the people whose dynasty produced Hammurabi of Babylon.

aphek.title: Aphek
aphek.note: The Philistines captured the ark of the covenant from Israel at Aphek. A later battle there went the other way, when Israel beat the Arameans after Elisha promised King Jehoash the victory.

aphiah.title: Aphiah
aphiah.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
aphiah.note: One of Saul's ancestors, named in the opening line of his genealogy and nowhere else.

ashdod.title: Ashdod
ashdod.note: Ashdod spelled another way, one of the five chief Philistine cities, on the coast between Ekron and Gaza. The captured ark was put in its temple of Dagon, and the affliction started there.

ashkelon.title: Ashkelon
ashkelon.note: One of the five main Philistine cities, a port on the coast midway between Gaza and Joppa. Samson killed thirty of its men there to pay off a wager. It is named on the Merneptah Stele, an Egyptian inscription from around 1208 BC.

ashtoreth.title: Ashtoreth
ashtoreth.about: A female deity in the Old Testament
ashtoreth.note: A Canaanite and Phoenician goddess of fertility and war, closely tied to Baal worship. Solomon built her a shrine late in his reign to please a foreign wife, and that is given as a main reason the kingdom split.

azzah.title: Azzah
azzah.note: Gaza, under a more literal spelling. The southernmost of the five chief Philistine cities, it sat on the coastal road between Egypt and Canaan.

baal.title: Baal
baal.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
baal.note: The Canaanite storm god, the power people believed sent the rain and made the crops grow. Worshipping him was the temptation Israel never shook, and the Old Testament fights it from the judges onward.

bechorath.title: Bechorath
bechorath.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
bechorath.note: Saul's family tree runs through him: son of Aphiah, an early forebear of Kish, Saul's father. The genealogy is there to set out Saul's Benjamite pedigree just before he comes on stage.

beer-shebah.title: Beer-shebah
beer-shebah.note: From Dan to Beersheba meant all of Israel, top to bottom, and this was the bottom. It marked the southern edge of Judah's land and went first to Simeon. Genesis gives two separate stories for how it got its name.

benjamin.title: Benjamin
benjamin.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
benjamin.note: Jacob's twelfth son and the youngest, born to Rachel on the road near Bethlehem as she died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him fiercely after losing Joseph. That fear drives much of the tension in Joseph's story.

beth-car.title: Beth-car
beth-car.note: It lay west of Mizpah, the point Israel chased the Philistines to after Samuel's victory. It was the same battle after which the stone Ebenezer went up.

beth-el.title: Beth-el
beth-el.note: About ten miles north of Jerusalem, and once the Canaanite city of Luz. Abram built an altar there. Jacob dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven there and called the place house of God.

beth-shemesh.title: Beth-shemesh
beth-shemesh.note: It was a Levitical city on Judah's northern border, its name meaning house of the sun. When the Philistines sent the ark back, it came here first and was welcomed with sacrifice.

bethshemite.title: Bethshemite
bethshemite.note: Someone from Beth-shemesh, a town of Judah near the Philistine border. When the Philistines sent the ark of the covenant back on a cart, it came to rest in a Bethshemite's field.

dagon.title: Dagon
dagon.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
dagon.note: The Philistines set the captured ark in Dagon's temple at Ashdod. His statue was found face down before the ark, and the second time it had lost its head and hands.

dan.title: Dan
dan.note: The tribe of Dan and the town it took. Squeezed in its first allotment near the Philistines, the tribe went north, captured Laish and renamed it Dan, Israel's northernmost town and the far end of from Dan to Beersheba. Jeroboam I put one of his golden calves there, and a stele from Tel Dan found in 1993 names the House of David.

ebenezer.title: Ebenezer
ebenezer.note: Stone of help. The Philistines first beat Israel near here and took the ark. Years later, after a win over the Philistines in the same area, Samuel set up a stone between Mizpah and Shen and gave it that name for the Lord's help.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

ekron.title: Ekron
ekron.note: Northernmost of the five Philistine cities, given to Judah and then Dan but never firmly held. The ark's last stop before the Philistines sent it back. Ahaziah of Israel sent there to ask Baal-zebub about his health, and an inscription at Tel Miqne naming Ikausu, or Achish, son of Padi settles the site.

ekronite.title: Ekronite
ekronite.note: Somebody from Ekron. When the ark arrived after the plagues at Ashdod and Gath, the Ekronites cried out in terror and demanded it go back to Israel.

eleazar-4.title: Eleazar
eleazar-4.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
eleazar-4.note: A man from the united kingdom, and 1 Samuel is the only book that names him.

eli.title: Eli
eli.about: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
eli.note: The high priest and judge at Shiloh who raised Samuel after Hannah gave him to the Lord. His sons stole sacrificial meat and slept with the women serving at the tabernacle door, and Eli only scolded them. Both died in the battle where the ark was taken, and Eli fell backward off his seat at the news and broke his neck, aged ninety-eight.

elihu-5.title: Elihu
elihu-5.about: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
elihu-5.note: 1 Samuel names him once, and he is a Levite from the united kingdom.

elkanah.title: Elkanah
elkanah.about: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
elkanah.note: Samuel's father. He had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah, and loved Hannah though she had no children and Peninnah taunted her for it. That is where Hannah's prayer for a son starts.

ephraim.title: Ephraim
ephraim.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephraim.note: Joseph's younger son. When Jacob blessed the two boys he crossed his hands on purpose and gave Ephraim the bigger blessing over Manasseh. The tribe came to dominate the north so much that the prophets use Ephraim for the whole northern kingdom.

ephraimite.title: Ephraimite
ephraimite.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephraimite.note: Someone of the tribe of Ephraim. In Judges 12 the men of Gilead caught Ephraimites at the fords by making them say shibboleth, and killed those who could not get the first sound right.

gath.title: Gath
gath.note: Goliath's hometown, one of the five Philistine cities. The captured ark brought disaster on it, David later hid there with King Achish while running from Saul, and in the end David took it. Most identify it with Tell es-Safi, where a potsherd turned up carrying two names related to Goliath.

gilgal.title: Gilgal
gilgal.note: Israel's first camp after crossing the Jordan. The people were circumcised there and kept their first Passover in the land, and later Samuel judged at Gilgal and Saul was confirmed as king there.

hannah.title: Hannah
hannah.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
hannah.note: Elkanah loved her, and she had no children, and his other wife Peninnah made sure she felt it. She prayed so hard and so silently at Shiloh that Eli thought she was drunk. Samuel was the answer, and she gave him to the Lord's service once he was weaned.

hophni.title: Hophni
hophni.about: Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
hophni.note: Eli's son, a priest at Shiloh, and a corrupt one. He and his brother Phinehas died in the battle where the Philistines took the Ark.

i-chabod.title: I-chabod
i-chabod.about: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
i-chabod.note: His mother named him as she died giving birth, having just heard that the ark was taken and that her husband Phinehas and his father Eli were both dead. The name means "no glory".

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

jehoshua-3.title: Jehoshua
jehoshua-3.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
jehoshua-3.note: One of 4 men called Jehoshua. This one is a man from the united kingdom, named twice in 1 Samuel.

jeroham.title: Jeroham
jeroham.about: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
jeroham.note: Samuel's family line goes back through him: he was the prophet's great-grandfather's generation, in the genealogy that opens 1 Samuel and again in the Levitical lists of Chronicles.

joel.title: Joel
joel.about: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
joel.note: Samuel's son, and not the prophet. Chronicles puts him in the Levite lists, and he is the father in a line of temple singers.

kirjath.title: Kirjath
kirjath.note: Kirjath-jearim, also called Baalah, a Gibeonite town on the line between Judah and Benjamin. The ark sat there twenty years after the Philistines gave it back, until David brought it up to Jerusalem. The prophet Uriah, whom Jehoiakim had killed, came from there.

kish.title: Kish
kish.about: Saul's father living at the time of United Monarchy
kish.note: Saul's father, a Benjamite of some standing. He lost his donkeys, sent Saul to find them, and the search ended with Samuel anointing Saul as Israel's first king.

matri.title: Matri
matri.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
matri.note: When the lot fell on Saul to be Israel's first king, it fell first on his family within Benjamin, the Matri, and that is the only time they are named.

mitspah.title: Mitspah
mitspah.note: A watchtower name, which is why so many places carry it. This one is where Jacob and Laban piled stones and agreed to keep apart.

peninnah.title: Peninnah
peninnah.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
peninnah.note: Elkanah's other wife. She had children while Hannah had none, and she taunted Hannah about it year after year, until Hannah's grief drove her to pray at Shiloh.

pharaoh.title: Pharaoh
pharaoh.note: The king Moses stood in front of. God sent Moses to him to bring Israel out of Egypt, and he hardened his heart through plague after plague before he let them go.

philistine.title: Philistine
philistine.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
philistine.note: Seafaring people who settled the coastal plain between Gezer and Gaza, most likely from Caphtor, which the Old Testament elsewhere identifies as Crete.

phinehas-2.title: Phinehas
phinehas-2.about: Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
phinehas-2.note: One of Eli's corrupt sons, killed in battle on the same day the Philistines captured the Ark of the Covenant.

rachel.title: Rachel
rachel.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
rachel.note: Jacob's favourite wife. He was tricked into marrying her older sister Leah first and had to work another seven years for Rachel. For years Leah bore son after son while Rachel had none.

ramathaimzophim.title: Ramathaimzophim
ramathaimzophim.note: The fuller form of Ramah, Samuel's hometown in the hill country of Ephraim. The "Zophim" part ties it to the clan of Zuph, his family.

samuel.title: Samuel
samuel.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
samuel.note: Hannah prayed for a son and gave him to the Lord before he was born. He grew up to be the last of the judges and the first great prophet. Israel's first two kings were both anointed by him.

saul.title: Saul
saul.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
saul.note: Israel's first king, found while he was out looking for his father's lost donkeys and anointed by Samuel in private before the tribes confirmed him.

shalim.title: Shalim
shalim.note: Saul came through the land of Shalim while he was hunting for his father's stray donkeys, before he was anointed king. Where exactly it lay is uncertain.

shalisha.title: Shalisha
shalisha.note: Saul passed through here looking for the lost donkeys too. The name means triple land, and the route puts it in the hill country of Ephraim.

shen.title: Shen
shen.note: A landmark, apparently a rock or ridge, between Mizpah and Jeshanah. After the Philistines were beaten in 1 Samuel 7, Samuel set up a stone between Mizpah and Shen.

shiloh.title: Shiloh
shiloh.note: The tabernacle stood at Shiloh, north of Bethel in Ephraim, for most of the time of the judges. Young Samuel served there. After the Philistines captured the ark, the place faded.

tabor.title: Tabor
tabor.note: A dome-shaped mountain rising out of the Jezreel Valley, on the line between Zebulun and Issachar. Deborah sent Barak there to gather Israel before the battle with Sisera. The psalmist sets it beside Hermon, and Hosea and Jeremiah both name it in oracles of judgment.

tohu.title: Tohu
tohu.about: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
tohu.note: Several generations back in Samuel's family line, before his father Elkanah.

zelzah.title: Zelzah
zelzah.note: It was a landmark in the sign Samuel gave Saul, a place near Rachel's tomb on the border of Benjamin.

zophai.title: Zophai
zophai.about: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
zophai.note: He was a Kohathite Levite and Samuel's ancestor, also spelled Zuph. The hill country where Elkanah's family lived was called the land of Zuph after him.

zophai-2.title: Zophai
zophai-2.note: Named once, in 1 Samuel, and nowhere else.
